steps.why: Two roles are all a short answer has room for, and these are the two that cover both kingdoms: chlorophyll is the plant role, and the phosphate-transferring enzymes are where magnesium acts in an animal cell.
common_mistakes: Writing Ca²⁺ as the ion of chlorophyll. The ion at the centre of chlorophyll is Mg²⁺.
Stopping at chlorophyll. Magnesium is needed by the enzymes of the ATP reactions as well.
steps.memory_tip: Magnesium: the green pigment of plants, and the enzymes of ATP.
steps.margin_note: Chlorophyll first, then the enzyme role; write ATP out in full once.

steps.why: Calcium is the ion of movement and repair. Clotting and muscle contraction are the two roles to name first; the nerve to muscle signal and the cell membrane follow from the same ion. Bones and teeth are where most of the calcium is stored, and storage is not the same as a role in a body fluid.
common_mistakes: Answering with bones and teeth alone. That is where calcium is stored; the question is about what the ion does, so name clotting and muscle contraction.
Giving chlorophyll to calcium. Chlorophyll belongs to magnesium.
steps.memory_tip: Clot, contract, signal, membrane — four things calcium is needed for.
steps.margin_note: Two or three named roles for calcium is a comfortable length.

insider_note: Keep the two ions on separate lines: magnesium with chlorophyll and the ATP enzymes, calcium with clotting, muscle and nerve.
